title: Build Your GitHub Portfolio
description: Set up a professional GitHub profile with a profile README, 5 pinned repos, and polished project documentation
objective: Students will create a professional GitHub profile with a profile README, pin their best repositories with polished READMEs including badges and screenshots, and verify their profile looks employer-ready

steps.title: Create Your GitHub Profile README
steps.instructions:
A **Profile README** is a special repository that displays on your GitHub profile page.

**Step 1:** Go to https://github.com/new

**Step 2:** Create a repository with the **exact same name as your GitHub username**.
- For example, if your username is `rahulsharma`, create a repo called `rahulsharma`
- Check "Add a README file"
- Click "Create repository"

**Step 3:** Edit the `README.md` with your professional introduction:

```markdown
## Hi, I am [Your Name] 👋

Full-stack Python developer from [Your City], India.
I build web applications with FastAPI, Django, and modern AI tools.

### What I Work With

**Languages:** Python, JavaScript, SQL, HTML, CSS
**Backend:** FastAPI, Django, Django REST Framework
**Database:** PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis
**AI/ML:** LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI
**DevOps:** Docker, GitHub Actions, Linux
**Tools:** Git, VS Code, Postman

### Featured Projects

| Project | Description | Tech | Link |
|---------|------------|------|------|
| SmartAttend | Student attendance with AI chatbot | FastAPI, LangChain | [Live](link) | [Code](link) |
| [Project 2] | [Description] | [Tech] | [Link] |
| [Project 3] | [Description] | [Tech] | [Link] |

### Currently
- Building full-stack AI products
- Open to full-time roles and freelance projects

### Contact
- Email: your.email@example.com
- LinkedIn: [Your Profile](https://linkedin.com/in/yourprofile)
```

Replace all placeholder text with your real information. Commit and push.

Visit your GitHub profile page — you should see the README displayed prominently.

steps.title: Polish Your Capstone Repository README
steps.instructions:
Open your capstone project repository on GitHub.

Replace the existing README.md with a professional version. Use this structure:

```markdown
# SmartAttend

> Student attendance management system with AI-powered chatbot for TechPath Institute

![CI](https://github.com/USERNAME/REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-blue)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.110-green)

## Live Demo
- **App:** [https://your-app.onrender.com](link)
- **API Docs:** [https://your-app.onrender.com/docs](link)

## Screenshots
![Dashboard](screenshots/dashboard.png)
![Mobile View](screenshots/mobile.png)

## Tech Stack
| Layer | Technology |
|-------|------------|
| Backend | FastAPI |
| Database | PostgreSQL |
| Frontend | HTML/CSS/JS + HTMX |
| AI | LangChain + OpenAI |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions |
| Hosting | Render |

## Quick Start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/USERNAME/REPO.git
cd REPO
cp .env.example .env
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

## Author
**Your Name** — [LinkedIn](link) | [GitHub](link)
```

**Important:** Add real screenshots!
1. Take screenshots of your app's key pages
2. Create a `screenshots/` folder in your repo
3. Add the PNG files and commit them
4. Reference them in your README

Push the changes and verify the README looks good on GitHub.

steps.title: Add Badges and Topics to All Repositories
steps.instructions:
For each of your pinned repositories, add:

**1. Repository Topics (Tags)**
- Go to your repo on GitHub
- Click the gear icon next to "About" (top right of the repo page)
- Add relevant topics: `python`, `fastapi`, `postgresql`, `langchain`, `rest-api`, `fullstack`
- Click "Save changes"

**2. About Description**
- In the same settings, add a short description (one sentence)
- Add your live demo URL in the "Website" field

**3. README Badges**
Add these badges at the top of each project README:

```markdown
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)
```

If you have GitHub Actions, add the CI badge:
```markdown
![CI](https://github.com/USERNAME/REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)
```

For custom badges, use https://shields.io:
- Select "Static" badge
- Enter label, message, and color
- Copy the markdown

**4. Add a LICENSE file**
- Go to your repo → Add file → Create new file
- Name it `LICENSE`
- GitHub will offer templates — choose "MIT License"
- Fill in your name and year
- Commit

Repeat for all 5 pinned repositories.

steps.title: Pin Your Best 5 Repositories
steps.instructions:
Go to your GitHub profile page (github.com/USERNAME).

Click **"Customize your pins"** (appears when you hover over the pinned section).

Select exactly 5 repositories to pin. Choose wisely:

| Slot | What to Pin | Example |
|------|------------|--------|
| 1 | **Capstone project** (most impressive) | SmartAttend |
| 2 | **Backend/API project** | A REST API you built |
| 3 | **Frontend project** | Portfolio website or interactive app |
| 4 | **AI/Data project** | RAG chatbot, data analysis tool |
| 5 | **Utility or course project** | CLI tool, automation script |

**If you don't have 5 strong repos yet**, create them now:
- Fork and customize a tutorial project
- Push a well-documented DSA practice repo
- Create a simple tool or script you actually use

After pinning, verify:
- [ ] All 5 repos have descriptions (visible on the pin card)
- [ ] At least 3 have stars (star your own repos as a baseline)
- [ ] At least 2 show recent commits (green activity indicator)
- [ ] At least 1 shows a language bar (Python, JavaScript, etc.)

Visit your profile in an incognito/private browser window to see how it looks to employers.

steps.title: Review and Verify Your Profile
steps.instructions:
Open your GitHub profile in a **private/incognito browser window** (to see it as a stranger would).

Go through this checklist:

**Profile Basics:**
- [ ] Profile photo is professional (clear face, not a meme or anime character)
- [ ] Display name is your real full name
- [ ] Bio mentions your role ("Python Developer" or "Full-Stack Developer")
- [ ] Location is set (e.g., "Bhopal, India")
- [ ] Profile README is visible and well-formatted

**Pinned Repositories:**
- [ ] Exactly 5 repos are pinned
- [ ] Each pin shows a description
- [ ] At least 3 have professional READMEs (check by clicking into each)
- [ ] At least 1 has a live demo link
- [ ] At least 1 has a CI badge

**Activity:**
- [ ] Contribution graph shows green squares in the last month
- [ ] Recent commits have meaningful messages (not "update" or "fix")

**Common Mistakes to Fix:**
- No `.env` files committed (check with `git log --all -- .env`)
- No `node_modules/` or `venv/` folders committed
- No empty repos pinned
- No repos with only an auto-generated README

If everything checks out, your GitHub profile is ready to share with employers and on your resume.

**Final step:** Copy your GitHub URL and add it to:
1. Your resume
2. Your LinkedIn profile
3. Your email signature

Your GitHub profile URL is: `https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME`

expected_output: A professional GitHub profile with a profile README displaying introduction and tech stack, 5 pinned repositories with polished READMEs including badges and screenshots, repository topics and descriptions set, and a clean contribution history visible to employers
